The return leg is on Tuesday at 14:00 CET at the Red Bull Football Academy. All tickets have already been snapped up. item.title: Real Madrid match blacked out on Chinese TV as Kylian Mbappe Mao Zedong meme controversy continues
item.description: Real Racing Club de Santander v Real Madrid - LaLiga EA Sports 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Real Madrid's commercial standing in Asia has taken significant hit as Chinese state television continued its refusal to broadcast the club's fixtures. The blackout follows the major fallout surrounding Kylian Mbappe and his controversial comments regarding former Chinese leader Mao Zedong. Mbappe comments lead to broadcast blackout The sporting relationship between Spain and China remains under immense strain as Chinese state broadcaster CCTV opted not to air Real Madrid’s recent 3-0 victory over Racing Santander . Despite Mbappe finding the net in that fixture, fans across China were unable to watch the action on the country's two main state-run sports channels. The controversy stems from a clip recorded in April that surfaced recently, showing the former PSG man laughing at a meme that superimposed his face onto an image of Mao. Describing the image as featuring "some guy" who he believed was a "Chinese dictator," Mbappe inadvertently sparked a geopolitical firestorm. While digital streaming platforms like Migu have continued to show some Spanish top-flight action, including Barcelona's recent 6-1 thrashing of Alaves , the Real Madrid fixture remained conspicuously absent from the schedules. This selective blackout suggests that the anger is specifically directed at Los Blancos and their talisman. Apologies fail to restore Chinese relations In the wake of the initial backlash, Mbappe issued a formal apology for what he described as "ill-judged" comments , while both Real Madrid and La Liga released statements expressing deep regret over the incident. These gestures were acknowledged by China's Ministry of Foreign Affairs, which stated it took the player’s contrition seriously. However, the diplomatic olive branch has not yet resulted in the restoration of broadcast rights on public television. The China Media Group had previously insisted that apologies from all three parties - the player, the club, and the league - were an absolute prerequisite for any movement toward a resolution. Even though these conditions were technically met, the continued absence of Real Madrid from CCTV screens suggests that the path to full redemption will be long and arduous. Financial and commercial impact for Mbappe Beyond the television blackout, the personal cost for Mbappe has been substantial. Several major Chinese brands moved quickly to terminate lucrative sponsorship deals with the forward as soon as the video gained traction. Furthermore, his presence on Chinese social media has been restricted, with his account on the popular Rednote platform being muted for violating community guidelines. This loss of digital presence significantly hampers his ability to engage with one of the world's largest fanbases. item.title: Travis Kelce reveals who was at fault for Kansas City Chiefs’ 28-24 defeat against Denver Broncos
item.description: Photo by Steph Chambers/Getty Images Travis Kelce has backed Andy Reid following the Kansas City Chiefs’ 28-24 defeat to the Denver Broncos, insisting the players must take responsibility for making their head coach’s decisions work. The Chiefs suffered their second consecutive loss after being beaten by Denver, with 11 penalties costing them 105 yards. The result also dropped Kansas City behind the Broncos in the AFC West standings. Kelce caught five passes for 62 yards but was unable to help his team avoid another frustrating defeat. Kansas City had a chance to take the lead late in the game, only for a false start penalty to wipe out a potential touchdown. Travis Kelce insists Kansas City Chiefs must execute Andy Reid’s plays Reid faced criticism for several decisions during the game, including sending Harrison Butker out to attempt a 54-yard field goal in rainy conditions on fourth-and-eight. His decision to keep left guard Kingsley Suamataia on the bench also raised questions. However, Kelce made it clear that he was not blaming the head coach for the defeat. “There’s a mentality that whatever Coach Reid calls, you got to find a way to get it into the end zone,” Kelce said. “And that’s the bottom line. That’s the mentality. And from here on out, it’s gotta be how we roll. And we have to execute.” The veteran tight end also acknowledged that he needed to improve his own performances as Kansas City attempts to turn its season around. “The reality of things is we got to fix a lot. The little things, mistakes, and it starts with the person you’re looking in the mirror, and I’m one of them,” Kelce said. He admitted to being frustrated with the procedural mistakes he has made over recent games, adding: “I gotta be better for my teammates. And that sets the tone for a lot of people in this room, and everybody’s just gotta up the ante from that.” Patrick Mahomes shared Kelce’s assessment, pointing to penalties, miscommunication and poor execution as reasons for the defeat. “We made big plays, and we made plays happen against a really good defense. But whenever you’re playing a team like that in the division, you’ve got to execute for the full 60 minutes, and we weren’t able to do that,” Mahomes said. Kansas City now turns its attention to the New York Jets in Week 9, with the Chiefs needing a response after consecutive defeats have left them chasing Denver in the AFC West. item.title: Pepe Mel, rushed into surgery after suffering a stroke
item.description: Pepe Mel, rushed into surgery after suffering a stroke A major scare for Spanish football. Legendary former Real Betis manager Pepe Mel has undergone emergency surgery in Seville after suffering a stroke this past Sunday. Fortunately, the surgery was successful. The 63-year-old Madrid-born coach is currently in the Intensive Care Unit (ICU), where he remains under observation as doctors monitor his progress over the coming hours. The news was announced through Real Betis Balompié's official channels. The club issued the statement at the direct request of the coach's family to keep fans fully informed. Mel is a true living legend at the club. As manager, he secured two promotions to the top flight and took the team back into European competition. Before that, as a player between 1989 and 1993, he had already won over the fans by scoring 58 goals. The coach, also much loved following spells at clubs such as Rayo Vallecano , Deportivo , Las Palmas and Tenerife , is already receiving a flood of messages of support from across the football world. item.title: 3 more takeaways from Kansas football’s Big 12 road loss against TCU
item.description: FORT WORTH, Texas — Kansas football’s opportunity at a Big 12 Conference road win came and went Saturday, against TCU. While the Jayhawks went into halftime up 13-0, they would go on to lose 22-16. Turnovers and other miscues in the second half sunk KU’s chances against the Horned Frogs. Ahead of a game Nov. 7 at home against UCF, Kansas (3-5, 1-4 in Big 12) once again has to regroup and find a way to generate some momentum to keep the hope of reaching a bowl game this fall alive. RELATED: Why Cole Ballard, not Isaiah Marshall, started at QB for KU football Here are a few more takeaways from KU’s loss against TCU: How did Kansas standouts Cam Pickett, Jalen Todd react to the loss? KU redshirt senior wide receiver Cam Pickett, who finished the game with 10 catches for 113 yards and a touchdown, acknowledged that people were frustrated in the locker room postgame. They felt like they should have been able to come away with a win. But he doesn’t think anyone lacks any confidence or trust in the group’s abilities, it’s just a matter of putting it all together for a full game. KU junior cornerback Jalen Todd noted it’s frustrating to have to deal with a recurring theme this year where the Jayhawks might start a game off well, but then not finish the job in the second half. He compared it to times when Kansas has fallen short in that regard the previous two seasons. In this matchup against TCU, Todd finished with five tackles and had a fumble recovery on special teams when a Horned Frogs returner muffed the catch on a punt. Was Lance Leipold surprised by TCU’s quarterback’s ability to run the ball? TCU fifth-year quarterback Jaden Craig finished with a season-high in rushing yards and attempts on the ground against Kansas. He ended up with 87 yards on 15 carries, not to mention a touchdown. That rushing score, from 17 yards out in the fourth quarter, helped put the Horned Frogs up 22-16. But KU coach Lance Leipold detailed that the Jayhawks anticipated Craig being used more in the running game. The issue, in Leipold’s mind, was wanting to have defended it better. Craig didn’t have much success consistently throwing the ball, and Todd allowed that was something Kansas focused on during the week of preparation ahead of kickoff. What does KU need to do next, to bounce back? Pickett detailed Leipold’s message to the team postgame was they need to keep moving forward, and not hang their heads. There are still going to be opportunities in the Big 12 to win each week. It’s just about sticking to something Leipold’s always talked about, the process, because there isn’t such a thing in Leipold’s mind as a winning week or a losing week when it comes to preparation. Todd also highlighted putting the TCU loss behind them and focusing on UCF. The season isn’t over yet. Kickoff for this upcoming weekend’s game against UCF is set for 2:45 p.m. (CT). item.title: Maryland serves as Purdue football's best, and maybe last, chance at victory
item.description: WEST LAFAYETTE − Barry Odom 's mantra all season has been that he wants Purdue football to be playing meaningful games in November. We've reached the final month of the regular season and, mathematically, Purdue is still bowl eligible, which seemed to be the basis of his statement. Right now there is no more meaningful game for the Boilermakers than Saturday, Nov. 7. It's homecoming and Purdue hosts Maryland, one of two teams in the Big Ten without a conference victory. The Terrapins are Purdue's best, and perhaps last, chance to get a victory this season. When the season began, the Boilermakers were picked to finish last in the USA Today preseason Big Ten poll . It was a cruel, but fair, projection. After all, Purdue had gone 0-9 in league play in consecutive seasons. To date, it's been Maryland and Michigan State relegated to the Big Ten's bottom feeders. A victory assures Purdue is no longer in that bottom pack and has elevated into the mucky middle behind the league's elite who are eyeing spots in the College Football Playoff and ahead of the Marylands, Michigan States and Rutgers of the league. At Purdue's best, it's in the upper echelon of that middle tier. But we've seen Purdue's best exactly once this season in a 41-13 win over Minnesota on Oct. 10. Since then, we've seen two lackluster performances against teams with comparable talent, resulting in a 38-26 loss to Washington and last Saturday's 31-17 loss at Penn State. More: Purdue football reality check: Penn State loss puts bowl hopes in jeopardy We saw Purdue's offense at its best at UCLA , which by the way is still unbeaten. The Boilers racked up nearly 500 yards on a day where unfortunately the defense was as inept as could be in a 52-38 loss. In the two most recent games, Purdue's thriving offense has been as drab as its defense was most of the season. So Odom's plea to play meaningful football games in November starts with the Boilermakers sitting at 3-5. Maryland, which has played inspired football in two one-score losses since firing coach Mike Locksley on Oct. 21, appears to be a "get right" game. For the Boilermakers, that's as meaningful as it gets when you look at a remaining schedule that includes games at Iowa and Indiana sandwiching the home finale against Wisconsin. That home game against the Badgers would be Purdue's best bet to secure another victory, but more than two decades of recent history tells us how those matchups turn out. Better Purdue teams have fallen to worse Wisconsin teams over an 18-game losing streak in the series dating back to 2004. What began as a bowl or bust season suddenly looks like a Maryland or nothing November. That'll be a hard sell to recruits and ticket purchasers the program is trending up. item.title: Loyola’s Sipes captures Shreveport Times AOW Week 6 football poll
item.description: Loyola’s Ryan Sipes garnered enough votes recently to win the seventh annual Shreveport Times online poll for Football Athlete of the Week , sponsored by Raising Cane’s Chicken Fingers, the Shreveport-Bossier Sports Commission and Silmon and Cosse Orthodontics. A lineman for the Flyers, Sipes made a strong run in winning the fifth football poll for the 2026-27 school year. He joins past winners that include North DeSoto’s Hayden Bell and Dakota Denney, along with Captain Shreve’s Gabe Lockett, Logansport’s Collin Magee and Benton’s Ryder Dodson. Sipes received 6,226 (48%) of the 16,729 votes cast in the online poll to top second-place Jacob Tibbett of Calvary, who finished with a tidy 4,260 votes (32.8%). Sipes will receive a backpack, a boxed lunch combo and some additional swag courtesy of Raising Cane’s and Cosse and Silmon. item.title: Andoni Iraola wishes Alexander Isak had done one thing differently in Liverpool defeat
item.description: Andoni Iraola wishes Alexander Isak had done one thing differently in Liverpool defeat Andoni Iraola is convinced that Liverpool would ‘100%’ have been awarded a penalty on Sunday if Alexander Isak had gone to ground after having his shirt pulled by Jurrien Timber. The Reds’ head coach was left bewildered over that incident in the 21st minute of the Reds’ 1-0 defeat at home to Arsenal, for whom Kai Havertz had scored just five minutes earlier. Neither Andy Madley nor the officials on VAR duty felt that a spot kick was warranted, a decision which was met with unified disagreement from Jamie Carragher, Ian Wright and Daniel Sturridge on Sky Sports. Iraola will tell Isak to go to ground in future Speaking to Sky Sports after the match, Iraola felt that the incident was a ‘clear penalty’ and believes that a foul would’ve been given had Isak gone down when Timber pulled his shirt. The Liverpool boss said: “The fact that you are even asking me that he should have gone to the floor, that’s the thing. If he goes to the floor, they call the penalty for me. They call the penalty 100%.” When the interviewer asked the Basque whether he’d tell Isak to go to ground if that happens again, he replied: “Yes, definitely.” Image via Sky Sports Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust Isak shouldn’t have to do the officials’ job for them We now have a farcical situation whereby Iraola feels compelled to openly advocate for his players to go to ground under contact from opponents because the officials on duty are failing in their task. Quite frankly, Isak shouldn’t feel any obligation to engineer a penalty in such situations, seeing as the shirt tug from Timber was so blatantly obvious that there’s no justification for those on VAR not to intervene, whatever about the on-field referee missing it. It’s the striker’s job to try and get on the end of the ball coming into the box (which he probably would’ve done if his jersey wasn’t pulled), not to seek the manufacturing of a spot kick because the officials can’t be trusted to do their job of calling such clear fouls. That decision felt significant in the overall context of the match yesterday. Had the referee awarded the penalty as he should’ve done, Liverpool would’ve had a chance to quickly cancel out Havertz’s goal. Had they done so, we can’t help but feel that it would’ve been a rather different game at Anfield. Obviously that’ll forever remain hypothetical, but there’s a real sense of what might’ve been had the officials not erred so badly over the incident involving Isak and Timber.

item.title: Liverpool draw up Virgil van Dijk contract plan as Reds make decision on captain's Anfield future
item.description: Liverpool v Chelsea - Carabao Cup Fourth Round - Getty Images Sport Liverpool are reportedly considering a new contract extension for captain Virgil van Dijk as his current deal nears its expiration. The club is eager to retain his immense leadership qualities while simultaneously negotiating a permanent transfer for Barcelona loanee Ronald Araujo. Contract talks on the horizon Liverpool are exploring the possibility of extending Van Dijk's contract at Anfield, as per TEAMtalk . The captain's current deal is set to expire at the end of the season, prompting internal discussions over his future. Despite turning 35, the veteran Dutch defender remains a vital component of the first team. He has featured for every single minute of their Premier League campaign so far this term. Liverpool deeply value his ongoing importance and want him to understand that a prolonged stay is welcome. A 12-month extension with additional options attached is reportedly among the structures currently under consideration. Iraola impressed by the captain Van Dijk’s incredibly consistent standards on and off the pitch have greatly impressed Andoni Iraola. The manager is highly satisfied with what the legendary centre-back brings to the dressing room. However, finalising an agreement may ultimately require a financial compromise. As one of the highest-earning defenders in European football, Van Dijk might need to accept a salary reduction to secure a new deal. According to the same report, both the club and the player are entirely open-minded about how the final structure could look. There is a mutual willingness to extend a remarkable stay that spans 10 seasons and 387 appearances. Guiding the next generation The club places immense value on Van Dijk's unique ability to mentor younger squad members. Emerging prospects like Jeremy Jacquet and Giovanni Leoni are directly benefiting from the captain's elite experience and high standards. While keeping their captain is crucial, Liverpool are simultaneously attempting to resolve other defensive situations. Negotiations are already underway with Barca to secure loanee Araujo on a permanent transfer. TEAMtalk suggest the final fee for Araujo could even be lower than the original agreement. Elsewhere, the club are weighing up a potential extension for Joe Gomez, though his extensive injury record remains a significant discussion factor. Looking towards the future For now, Van Dijk’s future is not viewed as an immediate cause for concern at Anfield. Sources indicate that a serious assessment of his contract situation will officially begin as the club moves into 2027. Both parties remain completely relaxed with the current state of affairs and are keeping an open dialogue. A short-term extension appears to be a highly realistic outcome as the new year quickly approaches.
